subject: [AMBER] Fortran runtime error: Bad value during integer read

messages.author: Sadaf Rani
messages.body:
Dear Amber users
I am getting an error of "Fortran runtime error: Bad value during integer
read" while running minimization. I am giving following command:-
sander -O -i min1.in -o min1.out -p complex_wild.prmtop -c
complex_wild.inpcrd -r min1.rst -ref complex_wild.prmtop
Min1.in is as follows:-
Minimization with Cartesian restraints for the solute
&cntrl
imin=1, maxcyc=100000,
ntmin=1, ncyc= 10000,
ntpr=5,
ntr=1,
&end
Group input for restrained atoms
25.0
RES 1 492
END
END
What is wrong in input that I am getting this error?
Any suggestions would be appreciated, please.
Regards
Sadaf

messages.author: Adrian Roitberg
messages.body:
I am not sure,  but start by moving your &end line one space to the left
to be aligned with your &cntrl line.
Adrian

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Fri, Jul 09, 2021, Sadaf Rani wrote:
>I am getting an error of "Fortran runtime error: Bad value during integer
>read" while running minimization. I am giving following command:-
>sander -O -i min1.in -o min1.out -p complex_wild.prmtop -c
>complex_wild.inpcrd -r min1.rst -ref complex_wild.prmtop
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
You are giving the prmtop file as input for the reference coordinates.
You need to put coordinates here, probably complex_wild.inpcrd.
Just a note: if you had included the "line 300 of set.F90" part of the
error, it would have been much easier for people to spot this sort of error.
It' always good to copy and paste the exact error message.
.....dac

messages.author: Sadaf Rani
messages.body:
Thank you DAC
It worked with -ref .inpcrd.
Regards
Sadaf
